test/task-list-filters.test.ts:193 ('rejects prose where a date belongs', from=ontem) and test/task-list-filters.test.ts:199 ('does not silently ignore an invalid date and return the whole list', from=nao-e-uma-data) assert the identical observable (res.status toBe 400, nothing else) against inputs in the same equivalence class: both are non-empty strings that fail isCalendarDate's leading YYYY-MM-DD-shaped regex check at the same branch, never reaching the Date round-trip check that makes the 2026-02-31 case (line 189) genuinely discriminative. Both sit under the same PRD AC-4 describe block (line 178). The 4-Task fixture seeded at line 200 (seedDateFixture()) is never read by any expect in the test, so it adds no discriminative power despite the name/comment framing a distinct silent-ignore defect mode: any implementation bug that fails one of these two tests fails the other identically, since isCalendarDate does not branch differently between the two input strings. Recommend dropping the redundant case or replacing it with a genuinely discriminative one, e.g. an empty from= value -- the actual 'absent parameter is never a filter' edge case the plan's Task 1(a) names, which the current suite does not otherwise exercise.

The replacement case (line 199, 'rejects an empty value rather than treating it as no filter', ?from=) is a genuinely distinct equivalence class from the three PRD-AC-4-named inputs beside it: 2026-8-1 and ontem are truthy strings, so a boundary check written from !== undefined && !isCalendarDate(from) (the plan's Task 1(a) shape) validates and correctly rejects both - but the empty string is falsy, so a plausible buggy boundary check written from && !isCalendarDate(from) (truthiness instead of !== undefined) would skip validation for '' and answer 200 while still correctly rejecting the other two.
